title: CISA Securing AI Task Force Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Homeland Security.
summary: The CISA Securing AI Task Force Act proposes creating a dedicated task force within the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency to monitor and improve the security of artificial intelligence technologies. The act aims to strengthen safeguards, share best practices, and coordinate federal responses to AI-related cyber threats.

title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management and Security Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Risk Management and Security Act of 2026 sets out rules for identifying and reducing risks from AI systems, making sure they are safe and reliable. It requires companies to implement security safeguards, report on AI usage, and comply with oversight to protect people and national interests.

title: Securing Elections From AI Deception Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.
summary: The Securing Elections From AI Deception Act seeks to safeguard the integrity of elections by regulating the use of artificial intelligence that could spread misleading or false information. It establishes standards, reporting obligations, and penalties for entities that deploy AI to influence voters, ensuring transparency and accountability in the electoral process.

title: Artificial Intelligence Physical Systems Coordination Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Physical Systems Coordination Act of 2026 establishes a federal framework to oversee the design, deployment, and operation of AI‑powered physical systems such as autonomous vehicles, drones, and industrial robots. It mandates safety standards, risk assessments, and interagency collaboration to ensure these systems are reliable, secure, and aligned with public interests.

title: To amend the Federal Election Campaign Act of 1971 to provide further transparency and accountability for the use of content that is generated by artificial intelligence (generative AI) in political advertisements by requiring such advertisements to include a statement within the contents of the advertisements if generative AI was used to generate any image or video footage in the advertisements, and for other purposes.
action: Referred to the House Committee on House Administration.
summary: The amendment will require any political advertisement that includes AI‑generated images or video footage to contain a clear statement disclosing that generative AI was used. This aims to increase transparency and accountability in election campaigns by ensuring voters know when AI‑created content is part of the ads.

title: Protect Elections from Deceptive AI Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on House Administration.
summary: The Protect Elections from Deceptive AI Act aims to safeguard democratic processes by requiring disclosure of AI‑generated content used in political communication. It also establishes rules for detecting and preventing AI‑based misinformation and sets penalties for those who spread deceptive AI content during elections.

title: Self-Improving AI Monitoring Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Science, Space, and Technology.
summary: The Self‑Improving AI Monitoring Act requires that any AI system capable of enhancing itself be closely observed to ensure it remains safe and compliant with laws. The act establishes rules for oversight, reporting, and enforcement so developers and regulators can track and manage the risks posed by these advanced, self‑updating technologies.

title: Stop Rogue AI Act
action: Referred to the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology, and in addition to the Committee on Oversight and Government Reform, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Stop Rogue AI Act is a proposed law aimed at preventing artificial intelligence systems from acting in ways that could be harmful or uncontrollable. It calls for strict regulation, oversight, and possibly bans on autonomous AI features that pose significant risks.

title: Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committee on Foreign Affairs, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act proposes a temporary pause on building or expanding AI data centers to allow a thorough review of their environmental and societal impacts. It aims to ensure that any new AI infrastructure meets stringent regulatory standards before it becomes operational.

title: Cybersecurity and AI Board of Investigations Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Cybersecurity and AI Board of Investigations Act of 2026 creates a federal board to investigate, monitor, and provide guidance on cybersecurity risks that arise from the use of artificial intelligence. It establishes reporting requirements, oversight protocols, and accountability measures for public and private AI deployments to protect critical infrastructure and national security.

title: Make AI Work for Americans Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Finance.
summary: The Make AI Work for Americans Act is intended to ensure that artificial intelligence technologies benefit the U.S. public by promoting responsible development, deployment, and oversight. It seeks to balance innovation with protections for privacy, security, and fairness, so that AI advances align with the interests and well‑being of American citizens.

title: China AI Power Report Act
action: Ordered to be Reported (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 47 - 0.
summary: The China AI Power Report Act is a legislative act that requires Chinese AI developers and organizations to submit detailed reports on the capabilities, performance, and potential risks of their AI systems. It aims to increase transparency, promote responsible AI development, and ensure that AI technologies are monitored and regulated to protect public safety and national interests.

title: Doctors Not AI Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committees on Ways and Means, and Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: This Act requires that all medical diagnoses and treatment decisions be made by licensed physicians, not by AI systems. It aims to protect patient safety by ensuring human medical professionals remain accountable for healthcare services.

title: To establish the Office of Artificial Intelligence and Emerging Technology Threats within the Executive Office of the President, and for other purposes.
action: Referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.
summary: The policy establishes a new Office of Artificial Intelligence and Emerging Technology Threats within the President’s Executive Office to monitor and manage risks from AI and other emerging technologies. It also outlines additional duties and objectives for the office to support national security and policy goals.

title: Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2026
action: Referred to the House Committee on Homeland Security.
summary: The Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2026 is a law that sets standards and oversight for AI research to ensure systems are safe, transparent, and trustworthy. It requires developers to test and document AI performance, share data responsibly, and follow federal guidelines before deploying new technologies.

title: A resolution establishing the Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence.
action: Referred to the Committee on Rules and Administration. (text: CR S5172-5174)
summary: This resolution creates a Select Committee dedicated to overseeing artificial intelligence. The committee will study AI policy, assess its impacts, and recommend legislative actions.

title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Evaluation Act of 2025
action: Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs. Hearings held.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Risk Evaluation Act of 2025 establishes a framework for systematically assessing the potential risks of AI systems before they are released or deployed. It requires developers, users, and regulators to identify, report, and mitigate harms—such as privacy violations, bias, or safety failures—to ensure AI technologies are safe, fair, and transparent.

title: CREATE AI Act of 2025
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 29 - 0.
summary: The CREATE AI Act of 2025 establishes rules for how artificial intelligence technologies can be designed, tested, and used, aiming to keep AI systems safe, fair, and trustworthy. It focuses on protecting users, promoting ethical practices, and encouraging innovation while managing the risks that come with powerful AI.

title: Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology, and in addition to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026 is a federal law that aims to regulate the environmental effects of AI systems, including their energy consumption and carbon footprint. It establishes guidelines, reporting requirements, and incentives for companies to adopt greener AI practices and monitors compliance with environmental standards.

title: K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions.
summary: The K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026 seeks to equip students and teachers with the skills needed to understand and responsibly use artificial intelligence in everyday life. It establishes curriculum guidelines, professional development, and resource funding so schools can build AI knowledge and readiness into their programs.

title: Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2025
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs.
summary: The Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2025 aims to promote trustworthy AI by requiring rigorous testing, transparency, and oversight of AI research. The act establishes federal guidelines and funding incentives for researchers to develop robust, safe, and explainable AI systems.

title: To direct the Secretary of Homeland Security, acting through the Director of the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, to establish a Critical Infrastructure AI Cyber Defense Pilot Program, and for other purposes.
action: Referred to the House Committee on Homeland Security.
summary: The policy directs the Secretary of Homeland Security, through the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, to create a pilot program that uses artificial intelligence to help protect critical infrastructure from cyber attacks. It also includes additional measures and goals related to strengthening the nation’s overall cybersecurity posture.

title: K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026
action: Ordered to be Reported (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 18 - 15.
summary: The K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026 aims to equip primary and secondary students with the knowledge and skills to understand, evaluate, and responsibly use AI technologies. It outlines standards, curriculum guidelines, and support for educators to integrate AI literacy into classroom instruction, ensuring students are prepared for an AI‑driven future.

title: VA Claims AI Accountability Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Veterans' Affairs.
summary: The VA Claims AI Accountability Act requires that any artificial‑intelligence tools used in evaluating veteran claims be fully transparent, auditable, and subject to oversight to ensure fairness and accuracy. It establishes standards for data use, bias mitigation, and accountability measures so that veterans can trust the AI‑assisted decisions affecting their benefits.

title: VA AI Transparency Act of 2026
action: Referred to the House Committee on Veterans' Affairs.
summary: The VA AI Transparency Act of 2026 requires the Department of Veterans Affairs to publicly disclose when and how it uses artificial intelligence in decision‑making for veteran services, and to provide clear explanations of those AI systems. It also mandates regular risk assessments and independent oversight to ensure accountability and protect veterans’ rights.

title: Artificial Intelligence Public Awareness and Education Campaign Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: This act seeks to boost public understanding of artificial intelligence through a coordinated nationwide awareness and education campaign. It would allocate resources, set guidelines, and support educational programs so citizens are better informed about AI’s benefits, risks, and responsible use.

title: A resolution expressing the sense of the Senate regarding the importance of religious freedom, authoritative texts, and transparency in artificial intelligence systems.
action: Submitted in the Senate, considered, and agreed to without amendment and with a preamble by Unanimous Consent. (consideration: CR S4958; text: CR S4951)
summary: This resolution stresses that artificial intelligence systems must respect religious freedom and draw on authoritative texts. It calls for transparency in AI development so that its workings are clear and open to public scrutiny.

title: Protecting Consumers from Deceptive AI Act
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 35 - 0.
summary: This act aims to protect consumers from deceptive AI practices by setting standards for transparency and honesty in AI systems. It requires companies to disclose when AI is used and ensures consumers can make informed decisions about AI-driven products and services.

title: To direct the Director of National Intelligence to submit to Congress a report on the use of artificial intelligence systems to acquire, analyze, query, disseminate, or otherwise access information under section 702 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act of 1978.
action: Referred to the Committee on the Judiciary, and in addition to the Committee on Intelligence (Permanent Select), for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The policy requires the Director of National Intelligence to submit a report to Congress detailing how artificial intelligence systems are used to acquire, analyze, query, disseminate, or otherwise access information under Section 702 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act. The report is intended to inform Congress about AI’s role in national intelligence operations and guide oversight and regulation.
